answer: A greyhound can reach about 64 to 72 km/h (40 to 45 mph) at full sprint, which makes it the fastest dog breed [1][2]. The highest officially timed speed is 67.32 km/h (41.83 mph), set by a greyhound named Star Title on a straight track in Wyong, Australia, in 1994 [1]. In races, winning dogs usually average about 58 to 61 km/h (36 to 38 mph) [2]. That puts a greyhound roughly 25 to 35 km/h slower than a cheetah's top speed. A greyhound can keep up its pace over longer distances than a cheetah, though, since a cheetah can only sprint in short bursts.
